title: Indole Test
principle: Detects the enzyme tryptophanase, which some organisms use to break down the amino acid tryptophan into indole, pyruvic acid, and ammonia. Indole reacts with Kovac's or Ehrlich's reagent (both containing p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde) to form a red/pink compound at the surface of the broth.
purpose: Commonly used within the broader IMViC test panel (Indole, Methyl Red, Voges-Proskauer, Citrate) to help differentiate Enterobacteriaceae, e.g. distinguishing Escherichia coli (typically indole-positive) from many other coliforms.

procedure.instruction: Inoculate a tryptophan-containing broth with the test organism and incubate at the appropriate temperature/duration for the organism.
Add several drops of Kovac's (or Ehrlich's) reagent to the surface of the broth culture.
Observe the color of the reagent layer at the broth surface within a minute or two of addition.

positiveResult: A red/pink ring or layer forms at the surface where the reagent was added.
negativeResult: The reagent layer remains its original color (typically yellow for Kovac's reagent) with no red ring.
interpretation: A positive result indicates tryptophanase activity and indole production; used alongside the rest of the IMViC panel rather than alone for identification.
precautions: Add reagent gently to avoid disturbing/mixing the broth before reading.
Handle Kovac's/Ehrlich's reagent (containing concentrated acid and an aldehyde) with appropriate PPE and ventilation.
limitations: A very lightly turbid/weak culture can give an ambiguous, faint reaction.
